verses.text: Job went on with his speech:
I wish I could go back to those earlier months, to the days when God watched over me.
His lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through the dark.
I was in my prime, and God’s friendship filled my tent.
The Almighty was still with me then, and my children were all around me.
My path flowed with butter, and even the rock poured out streams of oil for me.
I used to go to the city gate and take my seat in the public square.
The young men saw me and stepped out of sight. The elders got up and stood.
The leaders stopped talking and put their hands over their mouths.
The nobles fell quiet. Their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
Everyone who heard me blessed me, and everyone who saw me spoke well of me.
I rescued the poor who cried for help and the fatherless who had no one to stand up for them.
People who were close to dying blessed me, and I made widows sing for joy.
I wore righteousness like clothing. Justice was my robe and my crown.
I was eyes for the blind and feet for those who couldn’t walk.
I was a father to those in need, and I looked into the case of someone I didn’t even know.
I broke the jaws of the wicked and snatched their prey right out of their teeth.
I thought, ‘I’ll die in my own home, with days as countless as grains of sand.
My roots reach the water, and dew settles on my branches all night.
My honor stays fresh, and my bow is always strong in my hand.’
People listened to me and waited in silence for my advice.
After I spoke, no one had anything to add. My words sank in.
They waited for my words like people waiting for rain, taking them in like spring showers.
I smiled at them when they were losing heart, and they welcomed the light on my face.
I showed them which way to go and sat among them as their leader. I lived like a king among his troops and comforted people who were grieving.
